findings.evidence: `ConditionallyIIDWithFamily` at Family.lean:80 is the definition at ConditionallyIID/Basic.lean:72 with `ℕ` replaced by `ι`, and `ConditionallyIIDFamily` at Family.lean:149 similarly duplicates `ConditionallyIID` at Basic.lean:103; Family.lean:90–168 and 233–270 then duplicate or bridge the corresponding `intro`, `measurable_directing`, `jointLaw_eq_disintegration`, `of_directing`, and `exists_directing` APIs.
findings.fix: Generalize `ConditionallyIIDWith` and `ConditionallyIID` in `ConditionallyIID/Basic.lean` from `ℕ` to an inferred index type `ι`; existing sequence consumers will continue to infer `ι := ℕ`, while the countable-index theorem can use the same declarations directly. Retain only genuinely needed generic reindexing lemmas.
findings.issue: `ConditionallyIIDWithFamily` and `ConditionallyIIDFamily`, together with their constructors, accessors, reindexing lemmas, and ℕ comparison bridges, form a parallel copy of the existing conditional-IID API.

summary: The conditional family API duplicates the existing sequence API instead of generalizing it to an arbitrary index type.
